declared.title: Econometric Evidence for Satiation of Subjective Well-Being With Income at the Aggregate Level in Europe
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « happiness income satiation turning points around the world » (2026-11-22)

population: European countries, EU-SILC survey 2013 and 2018, net equivalised household income after taxes and transfers

findings.text: In Europe, life satisfaction and happiness stop rising above about 30,000 euros of net household income a year

support.sentence: At least for European countries, life satisfaction and happiness, two facets of SWB, show no further increase above 30,000 € net annual income (EDHI) both in 2013 and 2018.

findings.text: Only a few countries have crossed that threshold

support.sentence: Only a few countries have crossed the threshold and reached satiation.

limits: an aggregate-level analysis (« at the aggregate level »): about averages, not about individuals
cross-sectional: an association, not an effect of money
Europe only; kink regressions are sensitive to the threshold chosen (Lien 2016)
